paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2015 - Kaleido You Can Watch It But Cannot Record It
title: Kaleido: You Can Watch It But Cannot Record It
motivation: Film piracy causes $20.5B annual loss; over 90% of illegal online content comes from pirate movies captured by audience cameras
problem_framing: Maximize quality degradation of display-camera channel while retaining quality of screen-eye channel; opposite of screen-camera communication
key_insight: Exploit limited disparities between human vision (low-pass, temporal fusion) and camera (rolling shutter, sampling) to create imperceptible flicker for eyes but distorted recording for camera
method_signature: Re-encode video by decomposing frames into chromatic flickers above CFF and illuminance perturbations; human fuses, camera distorts
evaluation_criteria: Subjective survey (50 audiences, 5-point scale) plus objective metrics PSNR/SSIM/CD comparing original vs pirate video quality
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Cannot prevent high-quality pirate video by high-end professional cameras; leaves this as daunting challenge
evidence_for_taste: while do not affect the viewing experience of legitimate audiences
over 90% of the surveyed audiences do not see any quality differences
cannot recover original pixels using incomplete and distorted information
denoising attack cannot recover the original video
design to maximize the viewing experience
thinking_moves: 从communication系统的反向角度定义问题：不是最大化camera的解码能力，而是最大化camera的质量损失
把perception限制（CFF）当作安全编码的约束边界而非噪声
利用rolling shutter时序特性将信息失真从时域映射到空域（条纹伪影）
承认工程Trade-off：存在观看体验和防盗版之间的权衡
